clue.text: Rough one's uncouth, heartlessly dropping the aspirate

definitions.text: Rough one's uncouth, heartlessly dropping the aspirate

parts.words: Rough one's uncouth, heartlessly dropping the aspirate
parts.note: a rough gem is the idiom for a kind-hearted but unpolished person who drops his aitches; heartlessly hints at the card suit that is not hearts

explanation.surface: A coarse, unfeeling fellow who never sounds his aitches.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'a rough diamond' describes someone uncouth but good underneath, and 'heartlessly' teases with the red card suit that is not hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough one is the idiom for an unpolished person, and in cards it is the red suit other than hearts.

clue.text: The same but different? Editor wasn't sure

parts.note: do. short for ditto means the same

indicators.note: different means the word but is made different, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor asks whether something identical can also be different, and is unsure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' turns BUT into UBT, between DO (ditto) and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being uncertain about something is to have misgivings about it.

clue.text: Describing Hippolyta or the scene of the armadilloes' origin? Just so

definitions.meaning: Hippolyta was queen of the warrior women of Greek myth

definitions.text: the scene of the armadilloes' origin? Just so
definitions.meaning: Kipling's Just So Stories include The Beginning of the Armadilloes, set by the great South American river

explanation.surface: A question about a Greek queen or Kipling's armadillo story.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both the female warriors of Greek legend and the great rainforest river of Kipling's armadillo tale.

clue.text: It's obvious this urn is upset

indicators.note: this stands for the answer itself, so the answer with urn after it makes the word for upset, and removing urn leaves it

parts.note: to upset a vessel is to tip it upside down

explanation.surface: Plainly, this vase has been knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' means the answer: put it in front of URN and you get a word for upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain to see is open and not hidden, hence obvious.

clue.text: Enamoured if distracted in one's aspect

indicators.note: distracted means thrown into confusion, so the letters of enamoured are rearranged

explanation.surface: Being in love and distracted shows in one's face.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing or outward manner is the look a person presents, their aspect.

clue.text: Old man at sea as frisky as a lamb?

definitions.meaning: the old man is sailors' slang for the captain of a ship
a frisky lamb skips about, so it is one who skips

explanation.surface: An elderly sailor as lively as a spring lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's captain is called the old man, and a gambolling lamb is one that skips.

clue.text: Source of power way back West

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

indicators.note: back means the actress's first name is read backwards

parts.note: Mae West was an American film actress

explanation.surface: A source of energy along a road heading back west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' is not the direction but Mae West, the Hollywood star; 'back' turns MAE into EAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Vapour from boiling water drove engines and locomotives, a classic power source.

clue.text: Give prophylactic treatment to lion with acute distress

indicators.note: distress means the letters of lion and acute are put under strain and rearranged

explanation.surface: A vet vaccinating a lion that is in great pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To vaccinate someone is to give them preventive treatment against disease.

clue.text: Jack Merryman's object

definitions.meaning: Jack ... is the jester, a merryman, in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Yeomen of the Guard
object in the sense of purpose or aim

explanation.surface: Asking what a jester named Jack is aiming at.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera The Yeomen of the Guard features the strolling jester Jack, who sings The Merryman and His Maid.
explanation.definitionFit: The jester in the Savoy opera has this surname, and an aim or purpose is what something is for.

clue.text: Book tells what to do after initial fault

definitions.meaning: to book is to arrange in advance, as a table or seat

definitions.text: what to do after initial fault
definitions.meaning: in tennis a player who faults on the first service serves again

explanation.surface: A rulebook explains what to do after a first mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is read as RE-SERVE: tennis players get a second serve after a fault.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a seat is to set it aside in advance, and serving again is what a tennis player does after a fault.

clue.text: Custom America, say, rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters for say are read backwards

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: The United States turns down a traditional practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is established practice, the same as custom or habit.

clue.text: They help us to remember to put name, and income perhaps, in writing

indicators.note: in tells us the name and rearranged income are placed inside the writing

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the word income is only one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Advice to write down your name and earnings so you will not forget them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns INCOME into EMONIC; with N before it, that goes 'in' MS.
explanation.definitionFit: Memory aids such as rhymes and acronyms are devices that assist recall.

clue.text: Solicitor retains right to note "jolly fishy business"

indicators.note: retains means holds within, so the solicitor word keeps the right letter inside it

parts.note: a tout is one who solicits custom, not the lawyer the surface suggests
FA is a note of the sol-fa scale
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A lawyer keeps the right to send a memo about some dodgy dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a lawyer but is a TOUT; 'jolly' is a Royal Marine, RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish farm raising one kind of freshwater fish is literally a business dealing in fish.

clue.text: Speak such complete nonsense for instance

definitions.meaning: to speak is to voice or say aloud words
complete in the sense of absolute or total, as with nonsense

explanation.surface: Talking total rubbish, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such ... nonsense for instance' shows the second sense in use: one says total nonsense with this word.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something is to voice it, and the adjective means absolute or total, as in sheer nonsense.

clue.text: Meaning of leeway

definitions.meaning: meaning in the sense of gist, the general sense of what is said
leeway is a ship's sideways movement off course caused by wind

explanation.surface: A bare request for the sense of a nautical term.
explanation.definitionFit: The gist of an argument is its general sense, and a vessel carried sideways by wind or current is moving off course.

clue.text: Like a starlet emulating I ac

definitions.text: Like a starlet emulating I ac

parts.words: Like a starlet emulating I ac
parts.note: the nursery rhyme's little star shines like a gem in the sky, and 1 across is that gem

explanation.surface: A rising actress copying a crossword answer.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 ac' means 1 across, DIAMOND: 'Twinkle, twinkle, little star ... like a diamond in the sky'. 'Starlet' is read as a little star, not a young actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Little stars shine with a flickering light, as in the nursery rhyme.

clue.text: Banish for reversing carts into French river

indicators.note: into tells us the turned-round carts go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Oise is a river in northern France

indicators.note: reversing means the word carts is read backwards

explanation.surface: Driving carts backwards into a river in France gets you sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns CARTS into STRAC, which goes 'into' OISE after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude someone from society is to banish them, from the ancient Greek practice of exile by vote.

clue.text: Gold is in there perhaps, he speculates

indicators.note: in places the gold and is inside the rearranged there
perhaps shows the word there is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A prospector guesses that there may be gold in there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns THERE into THEER, and OR plus IS goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who forms theories is a person given to speculation.

clue.text: Urge single entry after this month

indicators.note: after shows that the single letter and the entry follow the abbreviation for this month

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means of this month in old business letters
I is the Roman numeral one, single
a gate is a way in, an entry

explanation.surface: Push for one entry to be made after the present month.
explanation.walkthrough: INST (instant) was commercial shorthand for 'this month', as in 'your letter of the 5th inst.'.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate is to incite or provoke, to urge something into action.

clue.text: In French Leave poor Eric is a janitor

indicators.note: In at the head of the clue places the rearranged name within the French word for leave

parts.note: conge is French for leave or dismissal

indicators.note: poor suggests the name Eric is in a bad way and so knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Eric, in a bad way while on French leave, works as a caretaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' turns ERIC into CIER, which goes 'In' CONGE, the French for leave; 'French leave' is an English idiom for slipping off unannounced.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorkeeper or caretaker of a French apartment building is the porter who looks after it.

clue.text: Sort of horse the battery may need?

definitions.meaning: a cavalry horse ridden into battle
a flat battery needs a device to restore its power

explanation.surface: An artillery battery may need a certain kind of horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Battery suggests artillery, which used horses, but the second sense is an electrical battery needing recharging.
explanation.definitionFit: A warhorse is a mount for battle, and a device that restores power to a flat cell is also so called.

clue.text: Comfort and money needed for the artist's support

parts.note: comfort means relief or rest
L stands for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Comfort and cash are what a painter needs to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's stand is a frame that holds the canvas while they work.

clue.text: Attract fish to rise on one side of the boat

definitions.text: on one side of the boat

indicators.note: rise in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to attract is to draw
the eel is a long snakelike fish

explanation.surface: Luring a fish up onto one side of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rise' turns DRAWEEL upwards, giving the whole answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The sheltered side of a vessel is the one away from the wind.

clue.text: Woeful expression caused by a deficiency

parts.note: a deficiency is a shortage or lack

explanation.surface: Someone sighing sadly because they are short of something.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic cry of sorrow or regret, like alas.

clue.text: Range, together with directions

parts.note: and means together with
E and S are compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: A range is spelled out together with directions.
explanation.definitionFit: The great mountain chain running down western South America is a range.

clue.text: Ripe green constituents of Smollett's Pickle

indicators.note: constituents of means the letters of the two words make up the answer in a new order

explanation.surface: Ripe green ingredients go into a pickle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents of' rearranges RIPE GREEN. Tobias Smollett wrote the 1751 novel The Adventures of Peregrine Pickle; the hero's surname is the misleading 'Pickle'.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Smollett's comic novel bears this first name before his surname.

clue.text: Origins of people lowly, even base, socially

definitions.text: Origins of people lowly, even base, socially

indicators.note: Origins of means the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Ordinary folk come from humble, even low, social origins.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as well as spelling it from its first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The common people of ancient Rome were the lowest social class.

clue.text: A defender in the van

definitions.meaning: one who protects or watches over
a train's official rides in the rear carriage called his van, and the vanguard is in the van of an army

explanation.surface: A soldier in the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry protects, and on a British train the official in charge rides in his own van.

clue.text: What actors learn, beset by mad dogs, shows highest quality

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the actors' words sit inside the jumbled dogs
mad suggests the word dogs is crazed and so jumbled

parts.note: actors learn their lines by heart

explanation.surface: Performers learning their parts surrounded by wild dogs show true virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' turns DOGS into GODS, which surrounds LINES ('beset by').
explanation.definitionFit: Being like God is piety, and holiness is reckoned the supreme virtue, next to cleanliness in the proverb.

clue.text: A magazine shows this lizard's retreat

indicators.note: retreat means go back, so the hidden letters are read backwards
shows means the letters are on display within the words A magazine

explanation.surface: A periodical features a reptile's hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'retreat' looks like the lizard's home but is the reversal signal; the letters 'shows' in A MAGAzine are read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A family of Old World lizards, including the frilled and bearded kinds.

clue.text: Head of staff breaks rules, quits job

indicators.note: breaks means cuts into, so that first letter sits inside the word for rules

parts.note: a monarch who rules reigns

indicators.note: Head of means the first letter of the word staff

explanation.surface: The chief of staff breaks regulations and walks out of the post.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up a post is to step down from it formally.

clue.text: Esau for instance — or a Muscovite chief?

definitions.meaning: Esau in Genesis was born red and hairy all over, an example of someone with ginger hair
a Soviet leader is a Red at the top

explanation.surface: Is the hairy brother of Jacob, or a Kremlin boss, being described?
explanation.definitionFit: Esau is a ginger-haired example, and a Communist leader in Moscow is the head of the Reds.
